title: Brain
subtitle: The organ that controls everything the body does
summary: A brain is a sheet of nerve cells, crumpled so it will fit, sitting on a stalk that already knew how to keep you breathing before anything in the sheet had a thought. The wrinkles are not decoration: they are how a square metre of cortex packs into a skull. The two halves talk through a bridge of white cable. The fluid-filled rooms inside are a shock absorber and a sewer.

parts.name: Left Hemisphere
parts.short: Language, for most people, lives here
parts.detail: A crumpled sheet of grey cortex over a core of white cables. In most right-handed people the regions that turn thought into words sit on this side. Damage here can take speech and leave the rest of the person intact, which is how we know the wrinkles are not all doing the same job.

parts.name: Right Hemisphere
parts.short: The other half of the same sheet
parts.detail: Not the 'creative side' in any way a textbook should still be saying. It handles the left visual field, much of attention, and a lot of what makes a face a face. Cut the bridge between the two and you get two minds in one skull, which is how we know they were talking.

parts.name: Cerebellum
parts.short: Finer wrinkles, and the reason you can catch a ball
parts.detail: Tucked under the back, with folia instead of gyri — the same trick at a smaller scale. It does not start movements; it times them. People without much of it can still decide to move, and then they miss.

parts.name: Brainstem
parts.short: The part that will not let you stop breathing
parts.detail: Midbrain, pons, medulla: a stalk of older machinery. Heart rate, blood pressure, the switch for consciousness. A hemisphere can be devastated and the person still live; this cannot.

parts.name: Corpus Callosum
parts.detail: Two hundred million fibres in a C-shaped bundle. Every time the left hand knows what the right is doing, this is why. Cut it to treat epilepsy and the two hemispheres go on as neighbours who no longer speak.

parts.name: Ventricles
parts.short: Rooms full of seawater, inside the brain
parts.detail: Four cavities making and circulating cerebrospinal fluid. The fluid is a cushion, a chemical bath, and a drain. If the drain blocks, the rooms swell and the brain is crushed from inside — hydrocephalus.

parts.name: Thalamus
parts.short: The relay: almost everything stops here first
parts.detail: Two egg-shaped nuclei on top of the brainstem. Sensory information, except smell, pauses here before cortex. Consciousness itself seems to need this loop. It is why a small stroke here can take a whole side of the world.

parts.name: Meninges
parts.short: Three skins, and the reason a skull blow can still bruise
parts.detail: Dura, arachnoid, pia: a tough outer bag, a web, a cling-film on the wrinkles. Between them runs the fluid. Meningitis is these skins inflamed. They enclose the whole organ, so they are drawn see-through.

parts.name: Cerebral Arteries
parts.short: A circle of blood under the brain
parts.detail: The circle of Willis and the trees that climb out of it. The brain is two percent of the body and takes twenty percent of the blood. A clot in one of these branches is a stroke, and the territory of that branch is the deficit.

parts.name: Pituitary
parts.short: A pea that runs the glands
parts.detail: Hanging from the hypothalamus on a stalk, in a bony saddle. It is not thinking. It is a bag of hormones that tells the thyroid, the adrenals and the gonads what to do. A tumour here can steal the visual fields from below because the optic chiasm sits on top of it.

parts.name: Olfactory Bulbs
parts.short: Smell is the one sense that skips the thalamus
parts.detail: Two stalks under the frontal lobes, plugged straight into cortex. That is why a smell can be a memory before you have a word for it. They are brain, not nose: the receptors in the nose are the only neurons that live in the weather.

parts.name: Spinal Cord
parts.detail: The brainstem continued, now with bone around it. Everything the body can tell the brain, and everything the brain can tell the body, funnels through this. Cut it and the person above the cut is intact, and the person below it is not.

steps.title: Crumple a sheet to fit a skull
steps.body: The cortex is a sheet. The sulci are how a square metre of it packs in. The two hemispheres are that sheet folded twice, with a gap down the middle.

steps.title: A cable between the halves
steps.body: The corpus callosum is why the halves are one mind. Cut it and they are two.

steps.title: Older machinery underneath
steps.body: The cerebellum times movement. The brainstem keeps you breathing whether you think about it or not. The thalamus is the relay the thinking sheet sits on.

steps.title: Rooms of fluid, a bag of skins
steps.body: Ventricles cushion and drain. Meninges enclose. Together they are why a brain can sit in a hard box without destroying itself at every nod.

steps.title: Fuel and a way out
steps.body: Arteries feed a greedy organ. The spinal cord is how anything that is not the head still counts as you.

quiz.prompt: Tap the cable that lets the two hemispheres talk.

choices: To pack a large sheet of nerve cells into a small skull
quiz.explain: Surface area. A smooth brain would need a much larger skull for the same sheet.
